issue.title: Approved-epic launch through sase monitor has never been exercised end to end; add a safe smoke harness
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-kp.12 (epic sase-kp, 'End-to-end monitor exercises') as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP, and filed here by sase-kp.land.

WHAT IS MISSING: epic sase-kp phase sase-kp.9 (commit 44796037a) rerouted approved-epic launches through the new monitor machinery: start_epic_launch_monitor() in src/sase/bead/epic_launch.py starts a monitor with the custom statuses EPIC APPROVED -> EPIC CREATED, reports the monitor id back to the approval surfaces, and keeps the old detached-task launch only as a fallback for when the planner lane cannot be resolved. That path has unit coverage, but it is the one monitor entry point in the whole epic that was never exercised against a real launch.

EVIDENCE: sase-kp.12 was the epic's end-to-end smoke phase and successfully drove every other monitor path with real launched agents -- completion plus follow-up handoff, non-zero exit, timeout enforcement and kill, stop with claim release, and list/show in rich, markdown, JSON, output-only, and follow modes. It could not drive this one. Its note records the reason: no EPIC APPROVED / EPIC CREATED monitor appeared anywhere in monitor history, and the phase could not manufacture one because epic phase workers are forbidden from creating beads. Re-confirmed by sase-kp.land on 2026-08-13: 'sase monitor list --all' returns five monitors, none with the epic-launch statuses.

WHY A HARNESS IS THE WORK: the obstacle is that a genuine exercise needs a real approved epic plan, which means writing to the durable bead store and launching real phase agents. The deliverable is therefore a repeatable, safe way to drive start_epic_launch_monitor() end to end without polluting the bead store or spawning real phase work -- for example a throwaway project or bead store plus a trivial single-phase plan, or a launch-approval fixture that stops after the monitor member is created.

SCOPE: (1) build the harness; (2) use it to assert the real observable behavior -- a monitor member is created for the approved epic, its start status is EPIC APPROVED and its stop status is EPIC CREATED, the approval surface receives the monitor id, and the monitor terminates cleanly; (3) exercise the documented fallback, i.e. an approval whose planner lane cannot be resolved still launches through the detached task path; (4) leave no durable beads, artifacts, or workspace claims behind.

RELATED CONTEXT: the four other defects sase-kp.12 found were all caused by the epic and are being fixed as sase-kp epic work before that epic closes; this one is a coverage gap rather than a defect, which is why it is filed separately.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-kp — the epic that introduced the untested path (phase sase-kp.9 rerouted approved-epic launches through sase monitor start; phase sase-kp.12 proposed this follow-up). Read sase-kp.9's and sase-kp.12's notes before starting.
